title: CLO Skills Mini-Class - Adjusting Strap Through Eyelet Buckle
description: CLO technical experts guide you in using accessories simulation to achieve a realistic adjustment strap buckle effect.
transcript:
How to Make a Pocket Strap  
Tips and Tricks  
Hi, everyone. This is Tips and Tricks.  
Today, I will show you how to make a pocket strap.  
Like the pocket, we also use the pocket to make a pocket strap.  
We can see the effect of the pocket strap on the pocket strap.  
Here is a real hole-in-the-box effect created using duplicate simulation.  
In the case of duplicate simulation, there is an interaction between the board and the duplicate.  
Currently, duplicate simulation can only be used in CPU simulation.  
So if you need to use duplicate simulation, it is recommended to switch to CPU simulation.  
We can see the hole-in-the-box effect on the left side.  
The goal is to pass a complete rope through this duplicate.  
Next, we need to pass this rope on the right side through a wooden buckle.  
To make it easier to operate, it is recommended to first divide this rope into three parts.  
You can use the hook and loop tool to divide the board.  
Divide it into three parts here.  
This also facilitates passing it through the board.  
Then add a fixed pin on the divided board.  
Turn on simulation.  
Then add a fixed pin here.  
This makes it easier to adjust the shape of the board and the position of the moving board.  
Next, add a wooden buckle.  
If you already have a corresponding duplicate solution,  
you can add it.  
You can also find a similar component in the CLOAD library or CONNECT.  
Add it to the 3D window and use it.  
Then here, we can copy the wooden buckle that we already have in the object window  
and drag it into the 3D window to add it.  
Here, we can use the positioning ball directly.  
Adjust the position of the wooden buckle using the positioning ball.  
Make the top board pass through the ring in the wooden buckle.  
You can see that this board has actually passed through the wooden buckle.  
So you can turn on simulation.  
Observe its buckle effect.  
You can see that the board and the duplicate are mutually interactive at this time.  
The board will hang on the duplicate,  
like the real buckle effect.  
We need to pay attention to duplicate simulation.  
There is a conflict between the board and the duplicate.  
Therefore, during the process,  
if the board and the duplicate overlap,  
you can use the selection tool to adjust the board to pass through.  
This prevents conflicts in the simulation between the board and the duplicate.  
If you see the area where there is overlap,  
you can use the selection tool to select it  
and use the positioning ball to adjust its position.  
So, the upper part of the wooden buckle is done.  
Then we assemble the upper part of the wooden buckle.  
You can adjust the remaining two parts of this strap.  
Because we have increased the thickness of the board,  
it is easier to observe  
the looping effect of the wooden buckle.  
You can switch to the clothing suspension type.  
Switch to the texture surface.  
Then here,  
we can see the pass-through effect of not only the thickness of the suspension.  
Let me remind you here:  
If there is deformation during the simulation process,  
it can also be adjusted in the attribute editor on the right.  
Adjust its rigidity.  
The greater the rigidity, the harder it is for the duplicate to deform.  
You can also adjust the thickness of the conflict.  
You can adjust the size of the gap between the duplicate and the board.  
Then create the looping effect of the strap.  
We can arrange this small board at the looping position on the wooden buckle  
and adjust its position using the positioning ball.  
Make it pass through the wooden buckle on one side.  
You can also switch to a different angle  
to check the effect on the board.  
Here we have arranged the position on one side.  
We can add an inner line here.  
Folding arrangement:  
Click on the 3D window,  
then use the internal multidirectional line tool  
to draw an inner line.  
Then select the folding arrangement tool in the 3D window.  
Select the inner line to fold.  
At the bottom,  
you can also add a new inner line and fold it.  
Arrange it.  
You can check whether there is any surface area.  
If there is, you can adjust the folding angle.  
At this point, the effect of this front buckle is also done.  
Then we can add the other two side boards.  
With the simulation open,  
use the fixed pin.  
Move the board position to the part that needs to be connected.  
Got it!  
Then we can remove all the pins on the board.  
Ok...  
Combine the boards together.  
Get ready for the next step.  
Open the simulation, check the cross-section of the board and the component, and adjust the cross-section area between the board and the component by selecting the grid tool.  
You can also select the cross-section area in the 2D window frame, and adjust the location of the area by using the positioning ball.  
In this way, the cross-section effect between the board and the component is completed.  
Since the rope belt is a complete board, we need to merge these three boards together to form a complete belt.  
Here you can also change the angle of these two cross-section lines to 180 degrees or delete these two internal lines.  
Finally, you can render the clothing type,  
and change it to the surface of the dense pattern.  
In this way, the thickness of the rope belt can also be displayed.  
Let's start the simulation again.  
In this way, the entire adjusted belt and the real cross-section effect are also done.

chunks.content: ## Overview of Pocket Strap Creation in CLO This section explains how to create a pocket strap using CLO software, focusing on simulation techniques, component integration, and detailed adjustments. Key concepts include duplicate simulation, board division, fixed pins, wooden buckles, and cross-section manipulation to achieve realistic strap behavior. --- ## Using Duplicate Simulation for Pocket Strap Effects Duplicate simulation in CLO enables interaction between the strap board and duplicates, creating realistic hole-in-the-box effects. Currently, duplicate simulation functions only in CPU simulation mode, so it is recommended to switch to CPU simulation when using this feature. - Duplicate simulation allows the strap board to interact physically with the buckle or ring. - This interaction simulates the strap hanging on the duplicate, mimicking a real buckle effect. - Conflicts may occur if the board and duplicate overlap; these must be manually adjusted using selection and positioning tools during simulation. --- ## Preparing the Strap Board for Assembly To facilitate manipulation and simulation, divide the strap board into three segments using the hook and loop tool. This segmentation makes it easier to pass the strap through the buckle and manage the fixed positions. - Divide the board into three parts for easier routing. - Add fixed pins to the divided segments to secure positions during simulation. - Turning on simulation after pin placement helps observe strap behavior and adjustments. --- ## Adding and Positioning the Wooden Buckle Component Incorporate a wooden buckle to simulate realistic strap connections: - Use an existing duplicate solution, or find a similar component in the CLOAD library or CONNECT. - Add the wooden buckle to the 3D window. - Use the positioning ball tool to adjust the buckle’s location and orientation precisely. - Pass the top board segment through the buckle ring to simulate threading. - Observe the interaction during simulation to ensure the strap hangs correctly on the buckle. --- ## Managing Board and Duplicate Conflicts During duplicate simulation, overlap between the board and duplicate may cause conflicts: - Use the selection tool to identify overlapping areas. - Adjust the board's position with the positioning ball to eliminate overlaps. - These adjustments maintain smooth simulation without unnatural clipping or penetration. --- ## Enhancing Strap Thickness and Visual Effects Increasing the board thickness improves visibility of the strap’s interaction with the buckle: - Switch to the clothing suspension type and texture surface mode for better visualization. - Adjust simulation attributes such as rigidity in the attribute editor to control deformation. - Higher rigidity makes duplicates less prone to deforming. - Modify the gap size between the duplicate and the strap board to fine-tune the simulation. --- ## Creating the Looping Effect on the Strap To form the strap loop around the wooden buckle: - Position a small board segment at the loop location. - Use the positioning ball to pass the strap through the buckle on one side. - Change viewing angles to verify correct strap placement and loop formation.

chunks.content: - Higher rigidity makes duplicates less prone to deforming. - Modify the gap size between the duplicate and the strap board to fine-tune the simulation. --- ## Creating the Looping Effect on the Strap To form the strap loop around the wooden buckle: - Position a small board segment at the loop location. - Use the positioning ball to pass the strap through the buckle on one side. - Change viewing angles to verify correct strap placement and loop formation. --- ## Adding Inner Lines and Folding for Realistic Detail Inner lines and folds create realistic strap bends and creases: - Use the internal multidirectional line tool in the 3D window to draw inner lines. - Apply the folding arrangement tool to fold the strap along these lines. - Add additional inner lines and fold them as needed. - Adjust folding angles to remove surface overlapping or unnatural creases. - These steps enhance the front buckle's detailed appearance. --- ## Assembling Side Boards and Finalizing Strap Shape Complete the strap by adding side board segments and combining all parts: - With simulation active, place fixed pins to position side boards at connection points. - After positioning, remove all pins to prepare for merging. - Combine the three board segments into a single continuous strap. - Adjust cross-section areas between the strap boards and components using the grid tool in 3D or 2D windows. - Modify the position of cross-section areas with the positioning ball for accuracy. --- ## Final Adjustments and Rendering Finalize the strap design with rendering and simulation checks: - Optionally, change cross-section line angles to 180 degrees or delete internal lines for a cleaner mesh. - Render the clothing type with a dense pattern surface to visualize strap thickness. - Restart simulation to observe the fully adjusted belt with realistic cross-section and looping effects. --- This process results in a pocket strap with accurate buckle interaction, realistic folding, and detailed thickness, suitable for high-fidelity CLO garment simulation and visualization.
